attacks.claim: The stored-data list omits the device name, which is personal data and is stored in sync.meta. The artifact's privacy claim is therefore contradicted by its own sync design.
attacks.evidence: 'sync.meta sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)' vs 'We store: Steam ID, Epic account ID, save blobs, sync.meta. No email, name, payment or friends data.'

attacks.claim: Retention for link history, access logs and backups after unlink or 24-month deletion is not specified, so the deletion claim cannot be verified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention period for link records, server access logs and deleted-data backups after 'Unlink and delete cloud saves'.

attacks.claim: Unlink is destructive (deletes all server copies), but the artifact does not require both store sessions or any confirmation for unlink. If linking is done with a compromised second-store login, the attacker could also delete the victim's cloud saves.
attacks.evidence: 'Linking requires valid sessions from both stores at the same time.' vs 'Unlink and delete cloud saves' removes the link and all server copies' with ABSENT: authentication requirement for unlink.

attacks.claim: The checksum is part of the untrusted blob, so it gives no integrity protection. The client parses attacker-controllable input before loading it, and the artifact does not say what parser or sandbox is used.
attacks.evidence: 'The client verifies the save's checksum and v3 schema before loading' with ABSENT: where the checksum key is held and whether it is signed or keyed.

attacks.claim: Age handling covers only Epic cabined accounts. Steam accounts of children under 13 or under the EU age-of-consent threshold are not gated, and consent is only a privacy-policy link shown before linking, not an affirmative, recorded consent.
attacks.evidence: 'Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts get a restricted status from EOS' and 'linked from the Cross-Save screen before linking' with ABSENT: age gate for Steam accounts and recorded consent step.

attacks.claim: Store-listing and policy compliance is asserted without evidence, including the Steam no-change claim and the Epic listing update.
attacks.evidence: 'Steam requires no listing change.' and 'Epic store page online features updated' with ABSENT: store-policy check or submitted listing evidence.

attacks.claim: The artifact says nothing is overwritten without a choice, but the launch path auto-downloads the cloud save whenever the local slot is judged older. 'Changed since last sync' and 'older' are undefined, so clock skew between PCs or stale sidecar timestamps can silently replace newer progress.
attacks.evidence: 'Nothing is overwritten without that choice.' vs 'the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older.' with ABSENT: definition of changed-since-last-sync and clock source.

attacks.claim: QA verified that 1.3 loads a 1.4 save, but not the return path: play on 1.3 (which does not update sidecar and may drop unknown options keys on re-save), then relaunch 1.4. That path could make the 1.3 progress look older and overwrite it.
attacks.evidence: 'a player moved back to 1.3 keeps a working save' and 'Loads, sidecar and modifier keys ignored' with ABSENT: 1.3-played save synced back into 1.4.

attacks.claim: The public patch note promises local saves stay put, but the auto-download path can replace the local slot on launch. The copy is misleading in a public, hard-to-retract channel.
attacks.evidence: 'Your saves on this PC stay where they are.' vs 'the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older.'

attacks.claim: Conflict prompt timestamps use 'today' without a time zone or date, which is ambiguous across time zones or midnight when two devices are involved.
attacks.evidence: 'Keep the save on this PC (12 h 41 m, today 18:02) or the cloud save (13 h 05 m, today 21:40)?'

attacks.claim: There is no evidence that players want cross-store sync. The beta measured opt-in on 2,300 players only, and discovery depends on opting in via Settings.
attacks.evidence: 'Off until a player turns it on in Settings > Cross-Save.' with ABSENT: demand or retention data.

attacks.claim: Linking requires two simultaneous store sign-ins, which adds friction and failure points for players on Steam Deck or controller-only setups.
attacks.evidence: 'Linking requires valid sessions from both stores at the same time.'

attacks.claim: No material accessibility attack. QA covered controller-only, keyboard-only, 200% scale and narration for the conflict prompt, though narration of the timestamps is not described.
attacks.evidence: 'screen narration for the conflict prompt' | Pass

attacks.claim: The load test (30k concurrent launches in 10 min) is far below patch-day demand. With 182k monthly players, 60% opt-in and all players launching 1.4 on Dec 2, the peak is not sized, and kill-switch config polling on every launch adds load.
attacks.evidence: '30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min' vs '~182k monthly active' and 'Dec 2 10:00 PT: 1.4 to all players on both stores'.

attacks.claim: Per-player limits do not bound total storage or egress. Free Epic accounts allow sybil bypass of the 60 uploads per hour and 10-slot limits, and the $600 hard stop disables the feature for everyone.
attacks.evidence: '60 uploads per hour per player' and 'hard project budget stop at $600/month; at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically'.

attacks.claim: The cost forecast is internally inconsistent and unsupported. 140 GB across about 109k opted-in players is about 1.3 MB each, which does not match 5 versions of 420 KB per slot across several slots. The $90 egress figure has no basis, and billing alerts lag by hours.
attacks.evidence: 'forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in, about $3/month. Requests and egress ~$90/month.' with ABSENT: per-player slot count assumption and billing latency.

attacks.claim: Sync uploads save slots and the sync.meta sidecar as separate operations, so a partial failure leaves a mismatched pair. The sidecar drives conflict decisions, so a partial upload can produce a wrong prompt or a wrong auto-download.
attacks.evidence: 'Sync uploads the existing save slots plus a small sync.meta sidecar' with ABSENT: atomicity or transactional commit.

attacks.claim: Alerts do not cover data-loss signals such as blob rejections, client load failures, or backup-restore rates at normal volume. A 2% error threshold at about 109k opted-in players can hide roughly 2,000 affected players.
attacks.evidence: 'Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%' with ABSENT: alerts on 'could not be read' events or per-player data-loss signals.

attacks.claim: The 24-month auto-deletion can remove the only remaining copy of a save with no warning, since no email is collected, which conflicts with the agreed 'never lose a save' rule.
attacks.evidence: 'Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted; if that player launches again, local saves are simply uploaded fresh.'

attacks.claim: The rollback to 1.3 is only tested on the Steam beta branch. The artifact asserts it for both stores, but Epic has no equivalent test, and Epic's default-branch model is not described.
attacks.evidence: 'Steam beta branch `1.3-legacy`' vs '1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores'.

attacks.claim: Release is all-at-once on both stores with no staged or canary rollout, so a sync or data bug reaches all players before a kill switch or revert can take effect.
attacks.evidence: '2. Dec 2 10:00 PT: 1.4 to all players on both stores; Cross-Save available to everyone who turns it on.'

attacks.claim: Retention is by count, not time. The 5 server versions and 3 local backups rotate out good saves within a few syncs of a buggy build, so 'every replaced version is kept' does not guarantee recovery of a good save.
attacks.evidence: 'the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot, and the game keeps the last 3 locally in saves/backup/'.

attacks.claim: The evidence is not from shipping artifacts or the public path. QA used a private Steam branch and an Epic dev sandbox build, and the Epic beta was only 150 sandbox testers, so the Epic public sync path was never exercised with real players.
attacks.evidence: 'Steam build 18204411 on a private branch, Epic build 1.4.0-cl5521 on the Epic dev sandbox' and 'Epic sandbox testers (150)'.

attacks.claim: Compatibility depends on the unverified behaviour of 1.3 (ignoring unknown options keys and sidecar) and on an ad hoc test matrix, with no documented contract for future versions.
attacks.evidence: 'Modifiers are stored in the existing v3 `options` map, whose unknown keys 1.3 already ignores.'

attacks.claim: The backend provider is not named, and the EU residency claim has no stated exit or self-host path. Identity depends entirely on Steam and Epic.
attacks.evidence: 'Storage region: EU (Frankfurt) for all players.' with ABSENT: provider name, exit plan or self-host option.

attacks.claim: Patch notes and the Steam/Epic news post go live simultaneously with the release, so public claims cannot be pulled back if the sync promise fails on launch day.
attacks.evidence: 'Patch notes + Steam/Epic news post: same time'

attacks.claim: The text says local-older saves are auto-replaced by the cloud copy, which contradicts the stated invariant that nothing is overwritten without a player choice. Staleness is judged from device-reported timestamps (last-modified, playtime), so a PC with a skewed clock can silently replace a newer local save. No compare-and-set or base-version check on upload is described either, so two devices syncing close together can overwrite each other's latest version.
attacks.evidence: "On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older." vs "Nothing is overwritten without that choice." ABSENT: base-version/ETag or compare-and-set on upload, and clock-skew handling for 'older'.

attacks.claim: The sidecar stores a device name, which is commonly personal data (e.g. a real name in a PC hostname). This contradicts the claim of no name data and is not disclosed in the privacy scope.
attacks.evidence: "sync.meta sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)" vs "No email, name, payment or friends data."

attacks.claim: Steam accounts have no described age gate. Only Epic cabined accounts are restricted, so under-13 Steam players can link and upload save data to the studio backend with no age check or parental consent path.
attacks.evidence: "Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts get a restricted status from EOS; for them linking is not offered" ABSENT: any age handling for Steam-side or non-cabined players.

attacks.claim: The patch-note copy promises local saves never move, but the sync design can download a newer cloud save over the local slot on launch. Players are told something false about data behaviour.
attacks.evidence: "Your saves on this PC stay where they are." vs "downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older."

attacks.claim: The client treats the checksum as integrity, but a checksum carries no authenticity. Anyone able to write to a player's slots with a valid token can compute a matching checksum and have the client parse attacker-chosen blob content on the next launch. The server also never parses blobs, so nothing validates content before it reaches the client parser.
attacks.evidence: "The client verifies the save's checksum and v3 schema before loading" and "the server never parses them" ABSENT: any authenticity or signing of stored blobs.

attacks.claim: The storage forecast does not state its slot-count assumption and appears to undercount. At the stated maximums (10 slots, 5 versions, 420 KB, 60% of 182k players) storage is about 2.3 TB, not 140 GB. The $600 auto-kill is tied to billing data that typically lags, and no mechanism is given for the hard stop taking effect in time.
attacks.evidence: "~420 KB per slot × up to 5 versions; forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in" and "10 slots per player" ABSENT: average slot count and the mechanism/latency for the budget kill switch.

attacks.claim: Epic, which is 29% of players, was validated only on a dev sandbox with 150 testers and an Epic build on the sandbox. EOS token validation against the production product configuration is untested, so linking could fail on release day for Epic players.
attacks.evidence: "Epic build 1.4.0-cl5521 on the Epic dev sandbox" and "Epic sandbox testers (150)" ABSENT: production EOS validation test or Epic production beta.

attacks.claim: Kill-switch re-enable or backend recovery would cause every opted-in client to hit sync at once, since the config is re-read every 10 min with no described backoff or jitter. Load was tested only at 30k concurrent over 10 min, below the scale of the full opted-in base.
attacks.evidence: "read on launch and every 10 min" and "30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min" ABSENT: retry backoff, jitter, or sync-storm limits.

attacks.claim: Alerts do not cover rejected or unreadable blobs or conflict-volume anomalies. A save-writing regression would reach players before anything fires.
attacks.evidence: "Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%, any spike in restores > 3× the beta rate."

attacks.claim: Conflict prompt times lack a timezone, so 'today 18:02' is ambiguous for players whose clock or region differs from the device.
attacks.evidence: "Keep the save on this PC (12 h 41 m, today 18:02) or the cloud save (13 h 05 m, today 21:40)?"

attacks.claim: Auto-download keyed on the 'older' timestamp can silently replace newer local progress when device clocks disagree, because last-modified comes from each device's own clock. This contradicts the 'nothing is overwritten without that choice' guarantee.
attacks.evidence: "On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older." vs "Nothing is overwritten without that choice." ABSENT: server-side time, clock-skew handling, or a rule that prompts on any timestamp disagreement.

attacks.claim: The sidecar stores a device name, which is personal data that can contain a real name. The privacy section says no name data is stored, so the stated data inventory is wrong and the privacy policy update may not cover it.
attacks.evidence: "sync.meta sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)" vs "No email, name, payment or friends data."

attacks.claim: The public patch note promises saves on this PC stay where they are, but the auto-download path can replace the local slot with no prompt. That is a misleading consumer-facing statement about the core promise.
attacks.evidence: "Your saves on this PC stay where they are." vs "the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older."

attacks.claim: Rollback to 1.3 leaves sync.meta stale because 1.3 ignores it and does not update it. When 1.4 returns, the local save can look older than cloud and be silently replaced, which is a data-loss path. The 'tested above' claim covers only loading in 1.3, not writing in 1.3 followed by re-sync. The only downgrade test is on the Steam beta branch, not Epic.
attacks.evidence: "1.3 ignores the sidecar, so a player moved back to 1.3 keeps a working save." and "1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores; saves written by 1.4 ... load in 1.3 (tested above)."

attacks.claim: The server never parses blobs and keeps only the last 5 versions per slot. A corrupt blob uploaded as the newest version becomes the cloud 'newest' and can push out good versions. Clients then keep rejecting it, and the recovery path is unspecified.
attacks.evidence: "Save blobs are treated as untrusted: the server never parses them" and "the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot" and "a blob that fails is not loaded, the previous version is kept"

attacks.claim: The Epic production path is not validated. Epic QA ran on the dev sandbox, and the Epic beta used sandbox testers only. Production EOS token validation and real production Epic accounts (including cabined accounts) are not evidenced, yet the QA claims production config.
attacks.evidence: "Epic build 1.4.0-cl5521 on the Epic dev sandbox" and "Epic sandbox testers (150)" vs "pointed at the production Cross-Save backend with the production config."

attacks.claim: Age gating covers only Epic cabined accounts. Steam accounts of minors can link and sync with no age check, and the privacy section does not address minors' consent for account linking and storage.
attacks.evidence: "Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts get a restricted status from EOS; for them linking is not offered" with no equivalent for Steam accounts or EU minors.

attacks.claim: Cost controls are weak. Steam and Epic accounts are free to create, and per-player quotas do not cap aggregate writes or storage. The $600 'hard budget stop' has no stated enforcement mechanism, and the kill switch keeps server copies and links, so storage keeps growing after the stop.
attacks.evidence: "hard project budget stop at $600/month; at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically" and "Server copies and links are kept so sync resumes". ABSENT: enforcement mechanism for the budget stop, and any global or per-IP write ceiling.

attacks.claim: The load test covers 30k concurrent launches over 10 minutes, but patch-day opt-in and conflict-prompt spikes are not modelled. The forecast also omits the 10-slot maximum from storage math.
attacks.evidence: "30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min" vs "forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in" and "10 slots per player".

attacks.claim: Monitoring lacks alerts on corrupt-blob rejections and kill-switch flips. Those are the earliest signals of silent data loss and of an incident that was resolved by disabling sync.
attacks.evidence: "Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%, any spike in restores > 3× the beta rate."

attacks.claim: The steam_id to epic_account_id mapping is a linkable identifier pair, but it is described as non-personal. Retention of the link itself after 24 months of inactivity is not specified, since only save data is deleted.
attacks.evidence: "Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted" and "We store: Steam ID, Epic account ID"

attacks.claim: The claim that Steam needs no listing change is asserted without support. The uniqueness rule for one link per account is also not described as atomic under concurrent link requests.
attacks.evidence: "Steam requires no listing change." and "Each store account can be in at most one link."
